sections.h2: Northglenn homes and who buys them
sections.html:
Northglenn lies north of Denver and spans Adams and Weld counties, covering about 7.4 square miles. It was built as a master planned community starting in 1959 and incorporated in 1969, so it has no railroad or farm town core. The population was 27,785 in 1970, dipped to 27,195 by 1990, and reached 38,131 in 2020. The city filled in early and grew slowly afterward, so a lot of its housing is original stock. The earliest houses are now more than 60 years old.

Expect older-house questions. How old are the roof and the sewer line? Are the windows original? Were past additions permitted? A financing buyer expects an inspection to flag these. A cash buyer simply folds them into the price and never asks you to arrange repairs.

Among owner-occupied homes only 0.8 percent sat vacant, against 7.3 percent of rentals, which tells you rentals are a meaningful part of the market. A house with a tenant is nothing unusual here. The RTD N Line connects the Northglenn/112th station to Downtown Denver, and a rail link is a feature a buyer can verify, so mention it when you describe the house.

sections.h2: Which county bills your Northglenn parcel?
sections.html: Most owners deal with Adams County, but parcels in the Weld portion are billed by the Weld County Treasurer. Read the county name on your tax bill before planning a payoff. That same county records your deed, and recording fees sent to the wrong one are not refunded.

MonthWhat happens
JanuaryTax notices are sent
FebruaryFirst-half payment due on the 28th, by receipt or postmark
AprilFull payment due on the 30th
JuneSecond-half payment due on the 15th
JulyDelinquent notices are mailed
SeptemberUnpaid real property taxes are advertised ahead of the tax lien sale
Late DecemberCommissioners certify the tax roll and set the mill levy

Each bill covers the prior year. Adams County takes a half payment or the full amount and nothing in between. If the tax is $25 or less, there is no half option and everything is due April 30. Anyone prepaying next year's tax has until noon on the last business day of December. An old unpaid balance can land in the fall tax lien sale, so clear it before you list.

Real property across Colorado is revalued every other year, in the odd-numbered ones, and Northglenn follows that cycle. The notice states the assessor's opinion of what your house is worth. Read it before pricing, and file it with your sale papers because buyers like to ask about the tax bill that comes next.

Title passes by a deed that the county clerk and recorder files. State law adds a documentary fee of 1 cent per $100 on any transfer above $500, and the deed has to list the buyer's mailing address.

  • Statute sets the recording fees, and they travel with the document.
  • Leave Social Security numbers off anything recorded, since the records are public.
  • Decide whether the filing goes to Adams or Weld before you mail it.

In a cash sale the title company usually takes care of this. Treat the list as a way to read your closing statement.

The climate is semi-arid, and the gap between the hottest and coldest days on record is large. Roofs, gutters, paint, furnaces and air conditioners take that punishment first. Owners who would rather not repair before closing often like a cash sale for that reason.

Listing puts a house in front of more buyers. A cash sale lets you set the closing date. Mention a tenant, a lien, an inherited title or deferred repairs when you call, and we will explain what each one does to the process and how an as-is purchase would handle it.

sections.h2: What a cash closing looks like
sections.html:
After you accept an offer, the title company confirms who owns the house, orders the tax certificate from the correct county and prepares the deed. You sign, the deed is recorded and the proceeds are paid after taxes and any loan are cleared. No lender appraisal is needed, so you and the buyer can pick a date.

Before you start, gather your latest tax notice, a mortgage payoff statement if a loan remains, and any repair or permit records. Heirs should line up proof of authority to sign. Landlords should have the lease and rent history ready, and should tell the buyer whether the tenant plans to stay. The more of this you hand over early, the fewer questions come up at the table.

Rentals are common enough here that buyers are used to them. Share the lease, the monthly rent and the end date, and say whether the tenant intends to stay. A buyer who keeps the tenant steps into the lease, so be exact about its terms. If you want the house empty, agree on a move-out date that fits the closing. Either way, the tenancy is part of the offer, so you do not have to clear the unit first.

Liens and unpaid balances turn up in the title search whether or not you mention them. Property taxes, an old mortgage and unpaid assessments all show up as items to be paid from your proceeds. Ask the county for the current tax balance and the lender for a payoff statement, so you can compare the total owed with the offer before you accept. If the numbers do not leave you enough, better to know on day one than at the signing.

Estates move faster when one person speaks for the family. Confirm who holds the authority to sign, collect the deed and the latest tax notice, and decide who will meet the title company. A house from the early years of the city may carry decades of deferred maintenance, and heirs rarely want to hire contractors for a property they do not plan to keep. A sale as-is lets everyone settle the estate on one date.

Whoever you sell to, ask the same few things. Is the offer in cash, and is there any condition besides clear title? Who pays for the title work and the recording? What date can the buyer close, and can that date move if your plans change? Will the buyer put the terms in writing before you commit? Straight answers tell you whether the offer is real, and a buyer who dodges them is giving you information too.

faqs.q: Is Northglenn in Adams County or Weld County?
faqs.a: Both. The county that holds your parcel bills the tax and records your deed, so check the county on your tax bill.

faqs.q: When are Adams County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due February 28, the second half June 15 and a full payment April 30. Adams County does not accept partial payments.

faqs.q: How far is Northglenn from downtown Denver by transit?
faqs.a: The RTD N Line runs from the Northglenn/112th station to Downtown Denver. Check RTD for current schedules and trip times.

faqs.q: What ZIP codes does Northglenn use?
faqs.a: 80233, 80234, 80241 and 80260. Use the one on your tax bill when you give an address to a title company.

faqs.q: Do I pay a state fee when I sell a house in Colorado?
faqs.a: Colorado charges a documentary fee of 1 cent per $100 on transfers above $500. Your closing statement will show the exact amount.
